name: The Peaks and Troughs of Life
description: Researcher Macadell of the institute seems to be troubled by something...

dialogs.content: Blast! Core output is still too inconsistent. My project is done for if it goes on like this...
What are you doing?
AAAAH! Y—You scared me! It could have turned messy had I pushed this button!
Judging by your look... You're not from the Adventurers' Guild.
Did you publish a commission with the Guild?
No, I don't have the money for that... And I'm no good at dealing with adventurers.
I'm just "collaborating" on a project with the Adventurers' Guild...
Oops, I forgot to introduce myself. I am Macadell, a researcher with the Fontaine Research Institute.
The project I worked on was the "Portable Mini Pneumousia Storage Device."
Thanks to the combined efforts of my fellow team members, we built the first prototype.
Then... Well, like everyone knows, a huge explosion occurred at the Institute.
The project leader and most of the members of the project team perished in the blast.
Apart from me, there's basically nobody else who can continue the work and push the research forward...
But... given the turmoil within the Institute, I must demonstrate its value as soon as possible in order to keep the project alive.
So, after consulting with all parties, the Adventurers' Guild and I reached an accord.
I wanted to use the prototype Portable Mini Pneumousia Storage Device as the core to create a Pressurized Impactor.
I wanted to use the operational performance of the Pressurized Impactors to prove the Portable Mini Pneumousia Storage Device's reliability.
And I did successfully build the machine, and began operating it.
Sounds like everything went fine.
Hahaha, yes, indeed... Until the Pressurized Impactor started running.
*sigh* I'd get a headache every time I talk about this.
I have no idea if the problem is with the prototype's design, or flaws in the Pressurized Impactor's method of energy transfer...
The power going from the Portable Mini Pneumousia Storage Device to the Pressurized Impactor always fluctuated wildly.
And that made the Impactor's output unpredictable as well!
When the output is high, this machine can easily crush rocks. But when output is low, even drilling a hole in mud is challenging.
Given the situation with the Institute, it was basically impossible for me to go back and rebuild the Portable Mini Pneumousia Storage Device...
I can only install an extra surveillance device on the prototype to monitor the strength of its energy output in real-time.
I just have to activate the Pressurized Impactor when the output is at its highest peak to maximize the potential!
That's way too convoluted!
But that's the best and cheapest solution I could think of... What else can I do?
*sigh* The Adventurers' Guild is probably thinking the same thing. That's why they haven't sent anyone yet...
What are we going to do? If we don't have the test data, I can't report back to the Institute...
Traveler, if you don't mind, could you help me out?
I assure you, my device is totally reliable! I even made a bunch of plug-ins for it that can enhance its various functionalities!
What if I can't get the timing right?
It's okay, the worst scenario is... that it doesn't have enough output. It won't blow up or anything.
All you have to do is wait for the next energy peak, then turn the machine on to get the maximum output.
Relax, Traveler. This machine is totally safe, and... after the test is over, I'll even pay you!
Then I'll leave it to you! My future, the future of this machine... And my future place in this project! It's all in your hands!
It won't blow up on me, will it?
That's absolutely not possible. I added a lot of safety and monitoring devices, so the worst case scenario that it doesn't have enough output. An explosion is impossible.
And even if you miss an energy peak, that's all right too.
Just wait for the next energy peak, then turn the machine on to get the maximum output.
That's not going to work...
Please don't say that! It's the best solution I've got. I swear, it's really useful!
That doesn't sound like a problem.
Yes, other than the machine itself, everything worked perfectly.
Did you hire adventurers for protection?
I can't afford them. They ask far too much for their services...
